name: Move
base_effect: Move one silhouette 0 object within short range.
narrative_capability: Can move objects up to silhouette 1 within medium range using the Force. With concentration, can hurl small objects with enough force to harm.
gm_choice_guidance: Offer telekinetic choices when physical objects could be manipulated at a distance. Lifting, pushing, pulling, catching, throwing. Scale to current upgrades — base Move cannot shift a starship.
dark_side_flavor: Dark side Move is violent. Objects don't drift — they slam. The Force doesn't suggest motion, it demands it.

range_1.name: Range
range_1.effect: Increase range of Move by one range band (short -> medium).
range_1.narrative: Reach further. The stone across the clearing. The tool on the far workbench. Distance was a wall, and it's thinning.

range_2.name: Range (Improved)
range_2.effect: Increase range of Move by another range band (medium -> long).
range_2.narrative: Distance is irrelevant now. What used to require proximity responds to intention alone.

strength_1.name: Strength
strength_1.effect: Increase silhouette of objects that can be moved by 1 (sil 0 -> sil 1).
strength_1.narrative: Push harder. Not just the stone but the boulder. Mass is resistance, and resistance can be overcome.

strength_2.name: Strength (Improved)
strength_2.effect: Increase silhouette of objects that can be moved by 1 (sil 1 -> sil 2).
strength_2.narrative: The weight of a speeder is nothing now. What once required straining concentration is routine.

control_hurl.name: Control: Hurl
control_hurl.effect: Can hurl objects to deal damage equal to silhouette x 10. Requires additional pip.
control_hurl.narrative: Think faster. The stone in mid-air, held and then redirected. The Force as reflex, not deliberation.

control_pull.name: Control: Fine Manipulation
control_pull.effect: Can perform fine manipulation at range — turning keys, pressing buttons, picking locks via the Force.
control_pull.narrative: Precision over power. The smallest movements require the most control, and control is what separates training from instinct.
